output.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2024,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2025 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2025,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2025 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END)
           - SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_increase_eur
FROM marts.fct_order_lines l
JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN marts.dim_products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE o.is_revenue
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY revenue_increase_eur DESC
LIMIT 1;
output.explanation: Revenue is taken at line level (fct_order_lines.net_amount) and restricted to completed orders (is_revenue = true) via the join to fct_orders, since order-level net_revenue cannot be split by product category. Each line is assigned to the calendar year of its order_date (fiscal year = calendar year), and category comes from dim_products. The query computes 2024 and 2025 revenue per category, the difference, and returns the category with the largest increase. Shipping fees are excluded because they are not in net_amount.
